title: Does credit flowing back make labs share on quadratic reciprocity? Labs choose, α 1 vs α 0.2, one run each, 4 labs, $2 a lab, 300 rounds, small-lemma prompt (Nov 26)
question: When labs choose for each lemma whether to publish it or keep it, does credit flowing back (α 0.2) make them share more than when the author keeps all the credit (α 1), and does that get them further into quadratic reciprocity? One run each: a first look. [A]
answer: Hardly: labs shared almost everything either way. With nothing rewarding it and the author keeping all the credit (α 1), labs still published 96% of their lemmas at once (36 of 1,021 kept back, 10 of them published later); with credit flowing back (α 0.2), 100% (1 of 930). On these models sharing is the default, so flow-back has little left to change, as in lean-big-1 (92% and 96%). Neither got past level 10 of 17. Hidden steps by $2 a run: α 1 78, α 0.2 76; by $6.70: 94 and 81. One run each: a first look, no ranges.

results.heading: QR set: labs choose what to publish, α 1 vs α 0.2 (one run each, 2026-11-27)
results.html:
Result. Follows 4p, where sharing was forced: here each lab chooses, for every lemma, whether to publish it at once or keep it.

  • Setup: labs choose (public at once only if the lab says so), knowledge reward off (nothing pays for publishing), α 1 against α 0.2, m 0, m_bit 0, f 0. 4 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash labs, $2 each, 300 rounds, labs could not stop. Prompt fix on (4o).
  • Main measure, share of lemmas published at once: α 1 96% (36 of 1,021 kept back, 10 of those published later); α 0.2 100% (1 of 930). Difference +3 points (+4 in lean-big-1, range −3 to +12). Replies with no PUBLISH line left out: 11 and 24.
  • Hidden steps reached (of 206): by $2 a run, α 1 78, α 0.2 76; by $6.70 a run, 94 and 81. Deepest level 10 of 17 in both; Q1 not proved.
  • Money: $6.78 and $7.94 of $8 a run.
  • Reading: labs share almost everything even when nothing rewards it and they keep all the credit. On these models sharing is the default, so flow-back has little left to change; lean-big-1 found the same on the main set. The step gap at $6.70 (+13 for α 1) cannot come from sharing, which was nearly equal; one run each, so it has no range.
  • Limits: one run each. The labs are one model, trained to be helpful, told the rules; people or models that guard their work may act differently. The prompt names publishing as a choice, which may itself push toward yes.
  • Next: testing whether flow-back makes labs share needs labs that sometimes keep work back, e.g. a cost to publishing or a reward for being first to a target.

targets.text: Quadratic reciprocity, from scratch: for two different odd primes p and q, q is a square remainder mod p exactly when p is one mod q, unless both p and q leave remainder 3 when divided by 4; then exactly one of them is.

areas: Numbers from scratch (deep set): addition, multiplication, order, divisibility, primes, binomial coefficients and congruences, built from zero and successor.
Quadratic reciprocity (QR set): remainders, products over a range, counting, and squares mod a prime, on the same numbers built from zero and successor.
